scope: Proposition 13.4 (Positive-time field inputs) of the manuscript “Critical mixing in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model” (preprints/Critical-mixing-in-the-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-model-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3ac6296cc238bae9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 88-89. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix 0 < s1 < T < ∞. There are positive constants ρ0, η0, ϵA, c0, c∗, a, depending on this interval, such that, at every deterministic s ∈ [s1, T], the 88 probability under the planted law, restricted to the original spectral event, of either failure of (13.1) or existence of y with ∥Fhs (y)∥ ≤ ρ0 √ n, q(y) < c∗ is at most e−an for sufficiently large n. The same assertion holds uniformly on each fixed compact interval after decreasing the residual threshold. There are also absolute c, C > 0 with the following small-time refinement. For each fixed A∗ > 0, at all sufficiently small r = √ s > 0, failure of (13.1) has probability at most e−A∗nr3 ; its margins may depend on the scale. For u ≥ Cr in a sufficiently small fixed range, existence of an approximate zero with q(y) > u has probability at most e−cnu3 . The approximate-zero tolerance is fixed before taking n → ∞ and may depend on s, u, A∗. Uniformity is asserted only on compact positive bands; finitely many or dyadic values of u may be imposed together. In the small-time assertions a vanishing maximum diagonal may be included in the external disorder restriction.
